Title: Purpose
Content: This procedure defines the requirements for monitoring, recording, and verifying the temperature of refrigerated and frozen product during receiving, storage, and shipping at Distribution Center DC-2. It is intended to maintain an unbroken cold chain and to provide a documented, repeatable basis for shipment hold and release decisions.

Title: Scope
Content: This SOP applies to all refrigerated and frozen finished goods received, stored, and shipped through DC-2 Cold Rooms A and B and Freezer F1. It covers receiving temperature checks, continuous storage monitoring, temperature excursions, and pre-shipment verification. It does not cover ambient dry-goods storage, which is addressed in SOP-WH-004.

Title: Cold Chain
Content: The uninterrupted series of temperature-controlled storage and handling steps that keep a product within its required temperature range from receipt through shipment.

Title: TOR (Time-Out-of-Refrigeration)
Content: The cumulative time a refrigerated product spends above 40 degrees F (4 degrees C) while outside controlled cold storage.

Title: Temperature Excursion
Content: Any recorded event in which a storage area's air temperature moves outside its validated setpoint range for more than 15 minutes.

Title: Setpoint
Content: The target air temperature a storage area is controlled to, distinct from the alarm limit at which corrective action begins.

Title: Cold-Chain Release
Content: The documented sign-off confirming a shipment met temperature requirements throughout storage and is cleared to ship.

Title: Data Logger
Content: A calibrated electronic device that records air or product temperature at fixed intervals.

Title: Receiving Clerk
Content: Measures and records product temperature at receipt and completes the Receiving Temperature Log before product is moved to storage.

Title: Cold Storage Operator
Content: Monitors area temperatures, responds to alarms, and records corrective actions on the Excursion Log.

Title: Warehouse QA Technician
Content: Performs pre-shipment temperature verification and approves or rejects shipments for cold-chain release.

Title: Shift Lead
Content: Confirms the shipping schedule, resolves cold-dock conflicts, and co-signs the Cold-Chain Release Record.

Title: Distribution Quality Lead
Content: Owns this SOP, reviews excursion and deviation reports, and approves any temporary variance to stated parameters.

Title: Calibrated data loggers
Content: One per storage area, logging air temperature at 15-minute intervals

Title: Handheld probe thermometer
Content: Calibrated; used for product core temperature checks

Title: Cold Rooms A and B
Content: Validated setpoint 36 degrees F (2 degrees C), acceptable range 34-40 degrees F

Title: Freezer F1
Content: Validated setpoint -10 degrees F, acceptable range -20 to 0 degrees F

Title: Cold-chain forms
Content: Excursion Log, Receiving Temperature Log, and Cold-Chain Release Record

Title: Step 1
Content: Receiving Clerk verifies that the carrier's transport temperature record accompanies the shipment.

Title: Step 2
Content: Measure the product core temperature of at least three cases per pallet using the calibrated probe thermometer.

Title: Step 3
Content: Refrigerated product must be at or below 40 degrees F to be accepted into Cold Rooms A/B; frozen product must be at or below 0 degrees F to be accepted into Freezer F1.

Title: Step 4
Content: Reject and quarantine any refrigerated shipment with a product core temperature above 45 degrees F; place it on hold pending disposition.

Title: Step 5
Content: Record all receiving temperatures on the Receiving Temperature Log before product is moved to storage.

Title: Step 6
Content: Each storage area is continuously monitored by a calibrated data logger recording air temperature every 15 minutes.

Title: Step 7
Content: Cold Storage Operator reviews logger readings at the start of every shift and records the review on the Storage Monitoring Log.

Title: Step 8
Content: Product core temperature is spot-checked and recorded every 4 hours for product staged on the cold dock.

Title: Step 9
Content: The cumulative time-out-of-refrigeration (TOR) for any refrigerated product staged outside cold storage must not exceed 2 hours.

Title: Step 10
Content: An area temperature outside its validated range for more than 15 minutes is a Temperature Excursion and triggers an alarm.

Title: Step 11
Content: Cold Storage Operator responds to the alarm, identifies the cause, and records the event and corrective action on the Excursion Log.

Title: Step 12
Content: Product exposed to an excursion is placed on hold and evaluated for disposition before it may ship.

Title: Step 13
Content: Warehouse QA Technician reviews the storage monitoring record for the shipment's storage period and confirms no unresolved excursion applies.

Title: Step 14
Content: Measure and record the product core temperature of a minimum of five cases from the outbound shipment.

Title: Step 15
Content: A refrigerated shipment passes when every measured case is at or below 40 degrees F; any case above 40 degrees F requires the shipment to be held and re-evaluated before release.
Parameter_Value: pass at or below 40 degrees F

Title: Step 16
Content: Warehouse QA Technician completes and signs the Cold-Chain Release Record; Shift Lead co-signs before the shipment may leave the dock.

Title: Product hold on failure
Content: Product affected by an excursion or a failed verification is placed on hold and evaluated for disposition before release.

Title: Two consecutive failures
Content: Two consecutive failed pre-shipment verifications on the same shipment trigger a documented deviation report and notification to the Distribution Quality Lead before a third attempt.

Title: Ship-before-pass recall
Content: Any shipment loaded before a passing verification is recorded is recalled from the dock and placed on hold.

Title: Repeated excursions
Content: Repeated excursions (3 or more in a rolling 30-day period) in the same storage area trigger a root-cause investigation per SOP-WH-030.

Title: Record Retention
Content: The Receiving Temperature Log, Storage Monitoring Log, Excursion Log, data logger exports, and Cold-Chain Release Records generated by this procedure are retained by Warehouse Operations for a minimum of 12 months from the date of creation.

Title: Training Requirements
Content: All personnel performing tasks under this SOP must complete cold-chain handling and temperature-monitoring training and demonstrate competency before working unsupervised. Refresher training is required annually and whenever this SOP is revised at a level that changes a stated parameter (temperature, time, or interval).
